purpose: Hard denominator for the repository claim that Davis--Kahan 1970 is 100% formalized.

selection_definition.counts_as_result: Exactly the four unnumbered Section 2 headline theorems and every named theorem, proposition, lemma, and corollary that Davis--Kahan actually establish in this paper.
selection_definition.statement_boundary: Only hypotheses, conclusions, and scope that belong to the printed result statement count. Setup, proof steps, examples, immediate consequences, and incidental later remarks remain source-fidelity material. A later source passage affects a counted result ONLY when it is necessary to determine what Davis and Kahan actually claim in that result under the paper's own semantics -- a standing convention, a definition, or a scope sentence the printed statement relies on. It does NOT enlarge the result merely because it discusses a stronger variant, an extension, a consequence, or another case. If such a passage is itself a distinct substantive result that Davis and Kahan introduce AND prove, it belongs in the denominator, and that is a decision for a fresh result-selection audit, not something the atom ledger may do on its own. CORRECTED 2026-08-31: this field previously ended "A later source passage that explicitly extends the proved scope of a counted result is part of that result's scope and must be covered", which contradicted `does_not_count`'s own entry for scope remarks outside the printed result environment and would have let the atom ledger enlarge the denominator by reclassification.
does_not_count: sharpness or interpretation commentary outside a designated result
immediate consequences or scope remarks outside the printed result environment
Section 10 open questions and their motivating special cases
claims explicitly left unresolved or whose proof is deferred to an open question
later proof-section restatements of a result already counted at its source statement
selection_definition.false_printed_result_policy: A designated result that is false remains in the denominator and is completed by exact formal refutation plus the repository best-effort repair obligation.

formalization_criterion.unit: The fundamental unit is a Davis--Kahan RESULT, not a source atom. Source-fidelity atoms exist so a hostile reviewer can audit the source-to-Lean correspondence; they do not independently create proof obligations.
formalization_criterion.membership: A source item belongs to the formalization denominator when Davis and Kahan present it as a mathematical result of the paper AND provide a proof for it. This is the four unnumbered Section 2 headline theorems plus the paper's proved named theorems, propositions, lemmas and corollaries. A fresh source audit may identify another genuinely independent proved result; definitions, proof steps, intermediate identities, examples, explanatory remarks, immediate consequences, restatements, and open or deferred claims do not become separate obligations merely because they contain mathematical assertions.
formalization_criterion.objective: Semantic equivalence of RESULTS, not reproduction of the paper's proofs. The Lean proof may use different lemmas, abstractions, representations, reductions, proof order, or stronger intermediate results. An intermediate step of the paper need not be separately formalized unless it is itself a counted result.
formalization_criterion.hostile_review_claim: For every counted result the repository must identify canonical Lean theorem evidence and support this claim: the hypotheses, mathematical objects, scope and conclusions of this Lean theorem are the same as those of the corresponding Davis--Kahan result, after making explicit any definitions or standing conventions the paper uses.
hostile_review_checklist: the precise angle, subspace, residual, perturbation or operator being bounded
real versus complex scalar scope where applicable
spectral-gap assumptions, including any half-infinite cases actually belonging to the result
standing assumptions or nonlocal conventions genuinely required by the paper
representative or multiplicity issues that affect unitarily invariant norms
formalization_criterion.equivalence_lemmas: Where a source formulation and the Lean formulation are equivalent but the equivalence is not apparent from the theorem types, an explicit correspondence lemma must be supplied.
formalization_criterion.terminal_certificate: Every substantive result introduced and proved by Davis and Kahan has canonical Lean evidence -- a proof, or an exact formal refutation where the printed result is false -- and every canonical Lean statement has been audited against the corresponding source result closely enough to withstand a hostile theorem-by-theorem comparison.
formalization_criterion.atoms_are_evidence_not_obligations: The source-atom inventory is deliberately far larger than the denominator. It is the evidence base for auditing the counted results, and a scope atom that records an extension, variant, consequence or another case is fidelity material, classified `result_adjacent_extension`.
